translations.literal: When the sacred person was failing, auspicious divination yielded nothing; he summoned us four ministers, together ascended the imperial couch, entrusted the testament and legacy, and committed state and household to us.
translations.idiomatic: When the sacred person was failing and no divination brought good omens, he summoned us four ministers to ascend the imperial couch together, entrusted us with his testament and legacy, and committed state and family to our care.

sentences.zh: 仰奉成旨，俯竭股肱，忠貞不效，期之以死。

translations.literal: Looking up we received his final charge; looking down we exhausted our limbs—if loyalty and fidelity did not succeed, we pledged ourselves to death.
translations.idiomatic: Looking up we received his final charge; looking down we gave our utmost—if loyalty and fidelity should fail, we were prepared to die for it.

sentences.zh: 但營陽悖德，自絕於天，社稷之危，憂在託付，不有所廢，將焉以興。

translations.literal: But Yingyang was depraved in virtue and cut himself off from Heaven; the altars were in peril and worry lay in what had been entrusted—without setting something aside, how could it rise?
translations.idiomatic: But Yingyang was depraved in virtue and cut himself off from Heaven; the altars stood in peril and the entrusted charge was at risk—without setting something aside, how could the dynasty rise?

sentences.zh: 乃遠稽殷、漢，用升聖德。

translations.literal: Thus we looked far back to Yin and Han and raised sacred virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Thus we looked far back to the precedents of Yin and Han and raised Your Majesty's sacred virtue to the throne.

sentences.zh: 陛下順流乘傳，不聽張武之疑，入邸龍飛，非俟宋昌之議，斯乃主臣相信，天人合契，九五當陽，化形四海。

translations.literal: Your Majesty rode downstream by post relay and did not heed Zhang Wu's doubts; entering the lodge, the dragon flew up without awaiting Song Chang's deliberation—this was lord and minister trusting each other, Heaven and man in accord; the nine-five line held the sun and transformed the form of the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty rode downstream by post relay and did not heed Zhang Wu's suspicions; entering the lodge, you ascended the throne without awaiting Song Chang's counsel—lord and minister trusting each other, Heaven and man in accord; you took the throne and your transforming influence reached the four seas.

sentences.zh: 羨之及亮，內贊皇猷，臣與道濟，分翰於外，普天之下，孰曰不宜。

translations.literal: Xianzhi and Liang supported the imperial design within; your servant and Daoji shouldered correspondence without—all under Heaven, who would say it was not fitting?
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi and Liang supported the imperial design within; your servant and Daoji shouldered affairs abroad—all under Heaven, who could say this arrangement was unfitting?

sentences.zh: 遂蒙寵授，來鎮此方，分留弟姪，以侍臺省。

translations.literal: Then we received favored appointment and came to guard this region, leaving behind younger brothers and nephews to attend at the central offices.
translations.idiomatic: Then we received favored appointment and came to guard this region, leaving behind younger brothers and nephews to serve at court.

sentences.zh: 到任以來，首尾三載，雖形在遠外，心係本朝，事無大小，動皆咨啟，八州之政，罔一專輒，尊上之心，足貫幽顯。

translations.literal: Since taking office, from first to last three years—though the body was far abroad, the heart was bound to the capital; in affairs great and small, every move was consulted and reported; in the eight provinces' administration, not one was our exclusive fiat; reverence for superiors sufficed to pierce the hidden and manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Since taking office, three full years have passed—though my body was far from the capital, my heart was bound to the court; in affairs great and small I reported every move; in governing eight provinces I never acted on my own authority; my reverence for Your Majesty reached from this world into the next.

sentences.zh: 陛下遠述先旨，申以婚姻，大息世休，復蒙引召，是以去年送女遣兒，闔家俱下，血誠如此，未知所愧。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, reaching back to the prior intent, strengthened it through marriage; your great son Shixiu again received summons to attend—thus last year we sent daughters and dispatched sons, the whole household coming down; sincerity in blood like this—I know not what to be ashamed of.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, honoring the prior intent, sealed it with marriage; your great son Shixiu was again summoned to court—thus last year we sent our daughters and sons, the whole household coming to the capital—such was our blood sincerity that I cannot imagine what we have to be ashamed of.

sentences.zh: 而凶狡無端，妄生釁禍，羨之內誅，臣受外伐，顧省諸懷，不識何罪？

translations.literal: Yet villains and cunning men without cause falsely stirred up calamity—Xianzhi was executed within, your servant was attacked without; examining all my inmost thoughts, what crime do I not recognize?
translations.idiomatic: Yet villains and cunning men without cause stirred up calamity—Xianzhi was executed within, your servant attacked from without; searching my inmost thoughts, I cannot see what crime I have committed.

sentences.zh: 天聽遐邈，陳訴靡由。

translations.literal: Heaven's hearing is far and remote; there is no way to lodge a plea.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's ear lies beyond reach; I have no avenue to present my plea.

sentences.zh: 弘等既蒙寵任，得侍左右，自謂勢擅狐鼠，理隔熏掘。

translations.literal: Hong and others, having received favored trust, attended at left and right; they considered themselves powerful as foxes and rats, and that reason blocked fumigation and excavation.
translations.idiomatic: Hong and others, having won favored trust, attended at Your Majesty's side; they deemed themselves omnipotent as foxes among rats, believing nothing could uproot them.

sentences.zh: 又以陛下富於春秋，始覽政事，欲馮陵恩幸，闚望國權，親從磐歭，規自封殖，不除臣等，罔得專權，所以交結讒慝，成是亂階。

translations.literal: Moreover, as Your Majesty is rich in years and has only begun to survey affairs of state, they wished to rely on favored fortune, peep at and covet state power, keep close attendants planted and thick, scheme to enrich themselves—unless we ministers were removed, they could not monopolize power; therefore they joined with slanderers and wicked men, making this the stairway to disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, as Your Majesty is still young and has only begun to govern, they wished to lean on imperial favor, covet state power, surround themselves with cronies, and enrich themselves—unless we ministers were removed they could not seize sole authority; so they joined with slanderers and wicked men, setting up the steps to rebellion.

sentences.zh: 又惟弘等所構，當以營陽為言，廬陵為罪。

translations.literal: Moreover, in what Hong and others fabricated, Yingyang was made the pretext and Luling the charge.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in their fabrications Hong and others used Yingyang as the pretext and Luling as the crime.

sentences.zh: 又以臣等位高功同，內外膠固。

translations.literal: Moreover, because we ministers held high rank and equal merit, inside and outside were glued fast.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, because we held high rank and equal merit, court and provinces stood as one.

sentences.zh: 陛下信其厚貌，忘厥左道，三至下機，能不暫惑。

translations.literal: Your Majesty trusted their thick outward appearances and forgot their perverse ways; thrice they descended to the loom—could you not be briefly deceived?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty trusted their plausible outward show and forgot their perverse arts; three times they set their snares—could you remain undeceived even for a moment?

sentences.zh: 伏自尋省，廢昏立明，事非為己。

translations.literal: Prostrate, I examine myself: deposing the blind and raising the enlightened—the matter was not for myself.
translations.idiomatic: Prostrate before my own conscience I see clearly: deposing the unworthy and raising the enlightened—I did this not for myself.

sentences.zh: 廬陵之事，不由傍人，內積蕭牆之釁，外行叔段之罰，既制之有主，臣何預焉。

translations.literal: In the matter of Luling, it was not from outsiders—within he accumulated trouble within the palace walls; without, the punishment of Shuduan was applied; since control had its master, what did your servant have to do with it?
translations.idiomatic: In the matter of Luling, outsiders had no hand in it—trouble was brewing within the palace walls, and the punishment of Shuduan was applied from without; since there was authority in charge, what part did your servant play?

sentences.zh: 然廬陵為性輕險，悌順不足，武皇臨崩，亦有口詔，比雖發自營陽，實非國禍。

translations.literal: Yet Luling by nature was light and rash, deficient in filial submission; when the Martial Emperor faced death, there was also an oral testament; though this time it arose from Yingyang, in truth it was no calamity to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Luling by nature was impulsive and rash, lacking in filial respect; when the Martial Emperor lay dying there was even an oral charge to that effect; though this affair arose under Yingyang, it was no true calamity to the state.

sentences.zh: 至於羨之、亮等，周旋同體，心腹內外，政欲戮力皇家，盡忠報主。

translations.literal: As for Xianzhi, Liang, and the others, moving together as one body, heart and belly within and without—they only wished to join strength for the imperial house and exhaust loyalty in serving their lord.
translations.idiomatic: As for Xianzhi, Liang, and the others, working as one within and without, heart and belly together—they wished only to join their strength for the imperial house and give their full loyalty to their lord.

sentences.zh: 若令臣等頗欲執權，不專為國，初廢營陽，陛下在遠，武皇之子，尚有童幼，擁以號令，誰敢非之。

translations.literal: If we ministers had greatly wished to grasp power and not devoted ourselves solely to the state, at the first deposition of Yingyang, when Your Majesty was far away, the Martial Emperor's sons still included infants—we could have held them up and issued commands; who would have dared oppose?
translations.idiomatic: If we had truly wished to seize power rather than serve the state alone, at the first deposition of Yingyang, when Your Majesty was far away and the Martial Emperor's sons still included infants, we could have placed one at the head and issued commands—who would have dared oppose?

sentences.zh: 而溯流三千，虛館三月，奉迎鑾駕，以遵下武，血心若斯，易為可鑒。

translations.literal: Yet we went upstream three thousand li, kept him in an empty lodge three months, welcomed the imperial carriage, and followed the precedent of the succeeding martial son—hearts in blood like this; how easy it is to take as mirror!
translations.idiomatic: Yet we traveled three thousand li upstream, kept him in an empty lodge three months, welcomed the imperial carriage, and honored the precedent of the succeeding sovereign—a heart in blood like this; what clearer proof could there be?

sentences.zh: 且臣等奉事先朝，十有七年，並居顯要，世稱恭謹，不圖一旦致茲釁罰。

translations.literal: Moreover, we served the former court seventeen years, all holding eminent posts, the age calling us reverent and careful—we never imagined we'd suddenly incur such punitive calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, we served the former court for seventeen years, all in eminent posts, renowned for reverence and care—who could have imagined we would suddenly suffer such punishment?

sentences.zh: 夫周公大賢，尚有流言之謗，伯奇至孝，不免譖愬之禍。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou, though a great sage, still suffered from slanderous rumors; Boqi, though supreme in filial piety, could not escape the calamity of false accusations.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou, greatest of sages, still suffered slanderous rumors; Boqi, paragon of filial piety, could not escape false accusation.

sentences.zh: 慈父非無情於仁子，明君豈有志於貞臣。

translations.literal: A loving father is not without feeling for a worthy son; a clear-sighted lord—how could he intend harm to loyal ministers?
translations.idiomatic: A loving father is not without feeling for a worthy son; how could a clear-sighted lord intend harm to loyal ministers?

sentences.zh: 奸遘所移，勢回山岳，況乃精誠微淺，而望求信者哉！

translations.literal: Moved by villainous encounters, momentum shifts mountains and hills—how much less could shallow sincerity hope to win trust!
translations.idiomatic: Moved by villainous encounters, even mountains can be overturned—how could my shallow sincerity hope to win belief!

sentences.zh: 《詩》不云乎：「讒人罔極，交亂四國。

translations.literal: Does not the Odes say: "The slanderer knows no limit, intersecting and disordering the four states.
translations.idiomatic: Does not the Odes say: "The slanderer knows no limit, intersecting and disordering the four states.

sentences.zh: 愷悌君子，無信讒言。」

translations.literal: The cordial and mild gentleman—do not believe slanderous words."
translations.idiomatic: The cordial and mild gentleman—do not believe slanderous words."

sentences.zh: 陛下躬覽篇籍，研覈是非，釁兆之萌，宜應深察。

translations.literal: Your Majesty personally reads the books, examining right and wrong—the first sprout of calamity ought to be deeply investigated.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty personally reads the classics and examines right from wrong—the first sprout of calamity should be scrutinized with care.

sentences.zh: 臣竊懼王室小有皇甫之患，大有閻樂之禍，夙夜殷憂，若無首領。

translations.literal: Your servant secretly fears for the royal house: a small calamity like Huangfu's, a great one like Yan Yue's—day and night in deep worry, as if without a head.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant secretly fears for the royal house a lesser disaster like Huangfu's, a greater like Yan Yue's—day and night in anguish, as though bereft of counsel.

sentences.zh: 夫周道浸微，桓、文稱伐，君側亂國，趙鞅入誅。

translations.literal: When Zhou's way sank into decline, Duke Huan and Duke Wen claimed punitive campaigns; those disordering the state at the ruler's side—Zhao Yang entered to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou way waned, Duke Huan and Duke Wen claimed punitive expeditions; when those beside the throne disorder the state, Zhao Yang enters to punish them.

sentences.zh: 況今凶禍滔天，辰極危逼，臺輔孥戮，岳牧傾陷。

translations.literal: How much more now, when vicious calamity floods Heaven, the pole star is perilously pressed, central ministers and families are slaughtered, and regional governors topple and fall.
translations.idiomatic: How much more now, when calamity floods the heavens, the throne itself is imperiled, chief ministers and their families are slaughtered, and regional governors are brought down.

sentences.zh: 臣才非絳侯，安漢是職，人愧博陸，廁奉遺旨。

translations.literal: Your servant's talent is not that of Lord Zhou; stabilizing Han was his office—in person I fall short of Lord Huo, yet I served among those who received the testament.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant is no Lord Zhou, whose office was to stabilize Han; I fall far short of Lord Huo, yet I stood among those who received the late emperor's testament.

sentences.zh: 國難既深，家痛亦切。

translations.literal: The state's difficulty is already deep; the family's grief is also acute.
translations.idiomatic: The state's crisis runs deep; the pain to my house is equally sharp.

sentences.zh: 輒簡徒繕甲，軍次巴陵，蕭欣窘懾，望風奔迸。

translations.literal: I then selected troops and repaired armor; the army halted at Baling; Xiao Xin, cramped and fearful, fled at the wind's report.
translations.idiomatic: I then mustered troops and repaired armor; the army encamped at Baling; Xiao Xin, stricken with fear, fled at the mere rumor of our approach.

sentences.zh: 臣誠短劣，在國忘身，仰憑社稷之靈，俯厲義勇之氣，將長驅電掃，直入石頭，梟翦元兇，誅夷首惡，弔二公之冤魂，寫私門之禍痛。

translations.literal: Though your servant is short and inferior, forgetting self for the state, looking up relying on the altars' spirits, looking down stirring righteous courage—I will drive long, sweep like lightning, enter straight to Stone City, behead and cut the chief villain, execute and destroy the ringleader, mourn the two lords' wronged souls, and inscribe my private household's calamity and pain.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am unworthy, I have forgotten self for the state; trusting in the spirits of the altars and steeling righteous resolve, I meant to drive straight like lightning into Stone City, cut down the chief villain, execute the ringleader, comfort the wronged souls of the two lords, and assuage the calamity that struck my household.

sentences.zh: 然後分歸司寇，甘赴鼎鑊，雖死之日，猶生之年。

translations.literal: Then I would separate and submit to the Minister of Crime, gladly going to the cauldron—though the day of death, it would be as a day of life.
translations.idiomatic: Then I would surrender myself to the Minister of Crime and gladly accept the cauldron—even my dying day would count as a day of living.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下德合乾元，道侔玄極，鑒凶禍之無端，察貞亮之有本，回日月之照，發霜電之威，梟四凶於廟庭，懸三監補絳闕，申二台之匪辜，明兩蕃之無罪，上謝祖宗，下告百姓，遣一乘之使，賜咫尺之書，臣便勒眾旋旗，還保所任。

translations.literal: Prostrate, I consider Your Majesty: virtue matching Qianyuan, the Way equal to the dark pole—discern that vicious calamity is groundless, see that loyalty and brightness have root; turn back the sun and moon's illumination, unleash frost and lightning's might; behead the Four Evils in the temple court, hang the Three Overseers to mend the crimson gate; declare the two chancellors' innocence, clarify the two frontier lords' guiltlessness; thank the ancestors above, inform the people below; send an envoy in a single carriage, grant a letter within arm's reach—your servant will then restrain the host, turn the banners, and return to guard his post.
translations.idiomatic: Prostrate before Your Majesty, whose virtue matches Heaven and whose Way equals the supreme pole—discern that this calamity is groundless, see that loyalty has its foundation; turn back the sun and moon's light, unleash the wrath of frost and lightning; execute the Four Evils in the temple court, hang the Three Overseers to restore the crimson gate; declare the two chancellors innocent and the two frontier lords guiltless; thank the ancestors above and inform the people below; send a single envoy with a letter within reach—and your servant will restrain his troops, turn his banners, and return to his post.

sentences.zh: 須次近路，尋複表聞。

translations.literal: I will halt at the near road and shortly again report by memorial.
translations.idiomatic: I shall pause on the near road and shortly submit another memorial.

sentences.zh: 初，晦與徐羨之、傅亮謀為自全之計，晦據上流，而檀道濟鎮廣陵，各有強兵，以制持朝廷；

translations.literal: At first, Hui with Xu Xianzhi and Fu Liang plotted a plan for self-preservation: Hui held the upper reaches while Tan Daoji guarded Guangling—each had strong troops to constrain and hold the court;
translations.idiomatic: At first Hui, together with Xu Xianzhi and Fu Liang, devised a plan for self-preservation: Hui held the upper Yangzi while Tan Daoji guarded Guangling—each commanded strong forces to hold the court in check;

sentences.zh: 羨之、亮於中秉權，可得持久。

translations.literal: Xianzhi and Liang wielded power within and could endure long.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi and Liang wielded power at court and could have held out indefinitely.

sentences.zh: 及太祖將行誅，王華之徒咸云：「道濟不可信。」

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor was about to carry out the executions, Wang Hua and his faction all said, "Daoji cannot be trusted."
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor was about to carry out the executions, Wang Hua and his faction all said, "Daoji cannot be trusted."

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「道濟止於脅從，本非事主。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor said, "Daoji was only coerced to follow; he was never the ringleader.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor said, "Daoji was only coerced to follow; he was never the ringleader.

sentences.zh: 殺害之事，又所不關。

translations.literal: The matter of killing was also nothing he was involved in.
translations.idiomatic: The killings were nothing he had a hand in.

sentences.zh: 吾召而問之，必異。」

translations.literal: If I summon and question him, he will surely differ."
translations.idiomatic: If I summon and question him, he will surely prove otherwise."

sentences.zh: 於是詔道濟入朝，授之以眾，委之西討。

translations.literal: Thereupon he issued an edict to Daoji to enter court, granted him troops, and entrusted him with the western campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he summoned Daoji to court, granted him troops, and entrusted him with the western campaign.

sentences.zh: 晦聞羨之等死，謂道濟必不獨全，及聞率眾來上，惶懼無計。

translations.literal: When Hui heard that Xianzhi and the others were dead, he judged that Daoji would surely not alone be spared; when he heard that Daoji was leading troops upstream, he was fearful and without plan.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui heard that Xianzhi and the others were dead, he assumed Daoji would not be spared alone; when he heard that Daoji was marching upstream with his army, he was stricken with fear and at a loss.

sentences.zh: 道濟既至，與彥之軍合，牽艦緣岸。

translations.literal: When Daoji arrived, he joined with Yanzhi's army and linked warships along the shore.
translations.idiomatic: When Daoji arrived, he joined forces with Yanzhi and linked warships along the shore.

sentences.zh: 晦始見艦數不多，輕之，不即出戰。

translations.literal: Hui at first saw the ships were not many, underestimated them, and did not immediately go out to battle.
translations.idiomatic: Hui at first saw that the enemy fleet was small, underestimated it, and did not immediately give battle.

sentences.zh: 至晚，因風帆上，前後連咽，西人離阻，無復闘心。

translations.literal: By evening, riding the wind with sails up, fore and aft linked throat to throat, the western men scattered and blocked, with no further will to fight.
translations.idiomatic: By evening, riding the wind with sails raised, the ships linked stem to stern; the western forces were scattered and cut off, and lost all will to fight.

sentences.zh: 臺軍至忌置洲尾，列艦過江，晦大軍一時潰散。

translations.literal: The imperial army reached Jizhi Zhouwei, deployed ships across the river, and Hui's great host collapsed all at once.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army reached the tail of Jizhi Isle, deployed ships across the river, and Hui's entire force collapsed in an instant.

sentences.zh: 晦夜出，投巴陵，得小船還江陵。

translations.literal: Hui went out by night, fled to Baling, obtained a small boat, and returned to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Hui fled by night to Baling, found a small boat, and returned to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 初，雍州刺史劉粹遣弟竟陵太守道濟與臺軍主沈敞之襲江陵，至沙橋，周超率萬餘人與戰，大破之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Inspector of Yongzhou Liu Cui had sent his younger brother Daoji, prefect of Jiling, together with the imperial army commander Shen Changzhi to raid Jiangling; reaching Shaqiao, Zhou Chao led more than ten thousand men to give battle and routed them decisively.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Inspector of Yongzhou Liu Cui had sent his younger brother Daoji, prefect of Jiling, together with imperial commander Shen Changzhi to raid Jiangling; at Shaqiao, Zhou Chao led more than ten thousand men into battle and routed them decisively.

sentences.zh: 俄而晦敗問至。

translations.literal: Soon word of Hui's defeat arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Soon word of Hui's defeat arrived.

sentences.zh: 晦至江陵，無它處分，唯愧謝周超而已。

translations.literal: When Hui reached Jiangling, he had no other disposition but to express shame and thank Zhou Chao, that was all.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui reached Jiangling, he could do nothing but express shame and apologize to Zhou Chao.

sentences.zh: 超其夜舍軍單舸詣到彥之降。

translations.literal: That night Zhou Chao abandoned his army, took a single boat, and went to Dao Yanzhi to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: That night Zhou Chao abandoned his army, took a single boat, and went to Dao Yanzhi to surrender.

sentences.zh: 眾散略盡，乃攜其弟遯、兄子世基等七騎北走。

translations.literal: The host scattered almost entirely; he then took his younger brother Dun, his elder brother's son Shiji, and six other riders to flee north.
translations.idiomatic: His forces scattered almost entirely; he then fled north with his younger brother Xie Dun, his elder brother's son Shiji, and five other riders—seven in all.

sentences.zh: 遯肥壯不能騎馬，晦每待之，行不得速。

translations.literal: Dun was fat and stout and could not ride a horse; Hui always waited for him, so they could not travel fast.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Dun was heavyset and could not ride; Hui always waited for him, so their flight could not be swift.

sentences.zh: 至安陸延頭，為戍主光順之所執。

translations.literal: Reaching Yantou in Anlu, he was seized by the garrison commander Guang Shunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Yantou in Anlu, he was seized by the garrison commander Guang Shunzhi.

sentences.zh: 順之，晦故吏也。

translations.literal: Shunzhi was Hui's former subordinate.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzhi had been Hui's former subordinate.

sentences.zh: 檻送京師，于路作《悲人道》，其詞曰：

translations.literal: Sent in a cage to the capital, on the road he composed "Lament for the Human Way," which reads:
translations.idiomatic: Sent to the capital in a cage, he composed on the road "Lament for the Human Way," which reads:

sentences.zh: 悲人道兮，悲人道之實難。

translations.literal: Alas for the human way! Alas—how truly hard is the human way.
translations.idiomatic: Alas for the human way! Alas—how truly hard is the path of being human.

sentences.zh: 哀人道之多險，傷人道之寡安。

translations.literal: Grieving that the human way has so many perils, lamenting that the human way offers little peace.
translations.idiomatic: I grieve that the path of humanity holds so many perils, and lament how seldom it offers peace.

sentences.zh: 懿華宗之冠胄，固清流而遠源。

translations.literal: Illustrious as the crown lineage of a noble clan, firmly a clear stream with distant source.
translations.idiomatic: Illustrious as the foremost lineage of a noble house, a clear stream with roots reaching far back.

sentences.zh: 樹文德於庭戶，立操學於衡門。

translations.literal: Planting literary virtue in courtyard and household, establishing moral learning at the balanced gate.
translations.idiomatic: They planted literary virtue within the household and established moral learning at the humble gate.

sentences.zh: 應積善之餘祐，當履福之所延。

translations.literal: One should inherit the surplus blessing of accumulated goodness and ought to tread where fortune extends.
translations.idiomatic: One should inherit the blessings of accumulated virtue and walk the path where fortune endures.

sentences.zh: 何小子之凶放，實招禍而作愆。

translations.literal: Why did this lowly fellow become so wicked and reckless—truly inviting calamity and committing offense?
translations.idiomatic: Why did this lowly fellow grow so wicked and reckless—truly inviting disaster and bringing guilt upon himself?

sentences.zh: 值革變之大運，遭一顧於聖皇。

translations.literal: Meeting the great fortune of revolutionary change, receiving a single glance from the sacred emperor.
translations.idiomatic: I met the great fortune of dynastic change and won a single glance of favor from the sacred emperor.

sentences.zh: 參謀猷於剙物，贊帝制於宏綱。

translations.literal: Participating in counsel at the founding of things, assisting the imperial system in its grand framework.
translations.idiomatic: I took part in counsel at the founding of the dynasty and helped shape the imperial order in its grand design.

sentences.zh: 出治戎於禁衛，入關言於帷房。

translations.literal: Without, governing arms among the palace guard; within, offering counsel in the curtained chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Without, I managed military affairs among the palace guard; within, I offered counsel in the curtained chamber.

sentences.zh: 分河山之珪組，繼文武之龜章。

translations.literal: Receiving jade seals and ribbons of rivers and mountains, continuing the turtle insignia of civil and martial honor.
translations.idiomatic: I received jade seals and ribbons granting rivers and mountains, and continued the turtle insignia of civil and martial honor.

sentences.zh: 稟顧命於西殿，受遺寄於御床。

translations.literal: Receiving the final charge in the western hall, accepting the testament's trust from the imperial couch.
translations.idiomatic: I received the final charge in the western hall and accepted the testament's trust from the imperial couch.

sentences.zh: 伊懦劣其無節，實懷此而不忘。

translations.literal: Though weak and inferior, lacking restraint, in truth I cherished this and did not forget.
translations.idiomatic: Though weak and lacking in virtue, I truly cherished this trust and never forgot it.

sentences.zh: 荷隆遇於先主，欲報之於後王。

translations.literal: Bearing great favor from the former lord, wishing to repay it under the succeeding king.
translations.idiomatic: I bore the late emperor's great favor and wished to repay it under his successor.

sentences.zh: 憂託付之無效，懼愧言於存亡。

translations.literal: Anxious that the entrusted charge had not succeeded, fearing shame before the living and the dead.
translations.idiomatic: I feared the entrusted charge had not been fulfilled and dreaded shame before the living and the dead.

sentences.zh: 謂繼體其嗣業，能增輝於前光。

translations.literal: Believing the successor would continue the inherited enterprise and could add luster to former glory.
translations.idiomatic: I believed the successor would continue the inherited enterprise and add luster to its former glory.

sentences.zh: 居遏密之未幾，越禮度而湎荒。

translations.literal: Dwelling in deep mourning not long, he transgressed ritual bounds and drowned in dissipation.
translations.idiomatic: Barely out of deep mourning, he transgressed ritual bounds and drowned in dissipation.

sentences.zh: 普天壤而殞氣，必社稷之淪喪。

translations.literal: All under heaven and earth would lose its breath—surely the altars would collapse and perish.
translations.idiomatic: All heaven and earth would lose its breath—the altars would surely collapse.

sentences.zh: 矧吾儕之體國，實啟處而匪遑。

translations.literal: How much more we who embody the state—in truth we could not rest easy in rising and dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: How much more we who embodied the state—we could not rest easy in our rising and dwelling.

sentences.zh: 藉億兆之一志，固昏極而明彰。

translations.literal: Relying on the myriad people's single will, firmly turning extreme darkness into clear brightness.
translations.idiomatic: Relying on the united will of the myriad people, we turned extreme darkness into clear light.

sentences.zh: 諒主尊而民晏，信卜祚之無疆。

translations.literal: Truly believing the lord would be honored and the people at peace, trusting the divined fortune was boundless.
translations.idiomatic: We trusted the sovereign would be honored and the people at peace, believing Heaven's mandate was boundless.

sentences.zh: 國既危而重構，家已衰而載昌。

translations.literal: Though the state was endangered it was rebuilt; though the house had declined it was borne to prosperity.
translations.idiomatic: Though the state was endangered it was rebuilt; though the house had declined it rose again to prosperity.

sentences.zh: 獲扶顧而休否，冀世道之方康。

translations.literal: We obtained support and looked to fortune's decline and rise, hoping the age's way was turning toward peace.
translations.idiomatic: We gained support and looked for fortune to turn, hoping the age was turning toward peace.

sentences.zh: 朝褒功以疏爵，祗命服於西蕃。

translations.literal: The court rewarded merit with enfeoffment; reverently I received appointment and served in the western frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The court rewarded merit with enfeoffment; reverently I received appointment and served on the western frontier.

sentences.zh: 奏簫管之嘈囋，擁朱旄之赫煌。

translations.literal: Pipe and flute music clamorous and resounding, bearing vermilion banners blazing bright.
translations.idiomatic: Pipe and flute music resounded; vermilion banners blazed in splendor.

sentences.zh: 臨八方以作鎮，響文武之桓桓。

translations.literal: Overlooking the eight directions as regional guardian, echoing the martial vigor of Wen and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: I stood as guardian over the eight directions, echoing the martial vigor of King Wen and King Wu.

sentences.zh: 厲薄弱以為政，實忘食於日旰。

translations.literal: Urging my weakness to govern, truly forgetting to eat until the sun slanted.
translations.idiomatic: I urged my weak self to govern, truly forgetting to eat until the sun was low in the sky.

sentences.zh: 豈申甫之敢慕，庶惟宋之屏翰。

translations.literal: How could I dare aspire to Shen Bo? I only hoped to be Song's screen and rampart.
translations.idiomatic: I dared not aspire to match Shen Bo; I only hoped to serve as Song's bulwark.

sentences.zh: 甫逾歷其三稔，實周回其未再。

translations.literal: Barely passing three full harvests, truly not yet completing two cycles round.
translations.idiomatic: Barely three full years had passed—not yet two full cycles round.

sentences.zh: 豈有慮於內囗囗囗囗其云裁。

translations.literal: How could there have been concerns within [damaged text in source] their pronouncements of guilt?
translations.idiomatic: How could there have been any design within [damaged text in source]—yet such pronouncements of guilt were raised?

sentences.zh: 痛夾輔之二宰，並加辟而靡貸。

translations.literal: Grieving the two chancellors who flanked and assisted—both were subjected to execution without mercy.
translations.idiomatic: I grieve for the two chancellors who flanked the throne—both were executed without mercy.

sentences.zh: 哀弱息之從禍，悲發中而心痗。

translations.literal: Lamenting my young sons who followed into calamity, grief rising from within and the heart afflicted.
translations.idiomatic: I lament my young sons who were swept into calamity; grief rises from within and my heart is wrung with pain.

sentences.zh: 伊荊漢之良彥，逮文武之子民。

translations.literal: These were worthy men of Jing and Han, reaching the civil and martial sons of the people.
translations.idiomatic: These were worthy men of Jing and Han, the civil and martial sons of the realm.

sentences.zh: 見忠貞而弗亮，睹理屈而莫申。

translations.literal: Seeing loyalty and fidelity yet not illuminating it, witnessing reason bent yet unable to declare it.
translations.idiomatic: They saw loyalty and fidelity yet could not make it clear; they witnessed injustice yet had no way to speak out.

sentences.zh: 皆義概而同憤，咸荷戈而競臻。

translations.literal: All shared righteous indignation and equal rage, each bearing weapons and racing to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: All shared righteous outrage and, bearing weapons, raced to join me.

sentences.zh: 浮舳艫之弈弈，陳車騎之轔轔。

translations.literal: Floating war-boats in dense array, deploying chariots and horsemen wheel on wheel.
translations.idiomatic: War-boats floated in dense array; chariots and horsemen deployed wheel on wheel.

sentences.zh: 觀人和與師整，謂茲兵其誰陳。

translations.literal: Observing the people's harmony and the army's order, I judged—against such forces, who could deploy opposition?
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the people's harmony and the army's discipline, I thought—against such a host, who could stand in our path?

sentences.zh: 庶亡魂之雪怨，反涇、渭於彝倫。

translations.literal: I hoped the departed souls would wash away their wrongs and restore Jing and Wei to proper human relations.
translations.idiomatic: I hoped the wronged dead would have their grievances cleared and that right order would be restored to the realm.

sentences.zh: 齊輕舟於江曲，殄銳敵其皆湮。

translations.literal: We arrayed light boats at the river's bend and destroyed the sharp foe until all were submerged.
translations.idiomatic: We arrayed light boats at the river's bend and wiped out the enemy's elite until none remained.

sentences.zh: 勒陸徒於白水，寇無反於隻輪。

translations.literal: We drove land troops at White Water; the foe returned not even with a single wheel.
translations.idiomatic: We drove our land forces at White Water; the enemy fled so utterly that not a single chariot wheel turned back.

sentences.zh: 氣有捷而益壯，威既肅而彌振。

translations.literal: Our spirit had swiftness and grew stronger; our awe was already stern and resounded all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Our spirit was swift and grew bolder; our authority was already stern and rang out all the louder.

sentences.zh: 嗟時哉之不與，迕風雨以逾旬。

translations.literal: Alas, the times did not favor us; we met wind and rain for more than ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Alas, fortune turned against us; wind and rain blocked us for more than ten days.

sentences.zh: 我謀戰而不克，彼繼奔其躡塵。

translations.literal: We planned battle but could not prevail; they pursued unceasingly, treading our dust.
translations.idiomatic: We planned for battle but could not win; they pressed the pursuit without pause, treading in our dust.

sentences.zh: 乏智勇之奇正，忽孟明而是遵。

translations.literal: Lacking the clever and brave use of orthodox and unorthodox tactics, suddenly we followed Meng Ming's path.
translations.idiomatic: We lacked the clever and brave alternation of orthodox and unorthodox tactics and suddenly went the way of Bai Mengming.

sentences.zh: 苟成敗其有數，豈怨天而尤人。

translations.literal: If success and failure have their allotted measure, how could one blame Heaven and reproach men?
translations.idiomatic: If victory and defeat have their allotted measure, how can one blame Heaven or reproach others?

sentences.zh: 恨矢石之未竭，遂摧師而覆陳。

translations.literal: I regret that arrows and stones were not yet exhausted; then the army was crushed and the formation overturned.
translations.idiomatic: I regret that our arrows and stones were not yet spent when the army was shattered and our battle lines overturned.

sentences.zh: 誠得喪之所遭，固當之其無吝。

translations.literal: Truly what gain and loss bring one to meet, one ought to bear without regret.
translations.idiomatic: What fortune and misfortune bring, one ought to accept without regret.

sentences.zh: 痛同懷之弱子，橫遭罹之殃釁。

translations.literal: I grieve the tender sons of the same womb who suffer calamity and offense unjustly.
translations.idiomatic: I grieve for the tender sons of my own flesh who were struck down by calamity through no fault of their own.

sentences.zh: 智未窮而事傾，力未極而莫振。

translations.literal: Wisdom was not yet exhausted yet affairs collapsed; strength was not yet at its limit yet could not be revived.
translations.idiomatic: My wisdom was not yet spent, yet the cause collapsed; my strength was not yet exhausted, yet nothing could be restored.

sentences.zh: 誓同盡於鋒鏑，我怯力而愆信。

translations.literal: We swore to die together at arrow-point; I was weak in strength and failed in faith.
translations.idiomatic: We swore to die together under the blades; I was weak in courage and failed in my pledge.

sentences.zh: 愍弟姪之何辜，實吾咎之所嬰。

translations.literal: I pity what guilt my younger brothers and nephews have; truly it is my fault that ensnares them.
translations.idiomatic: I pity my younger brothers and nephews—what guilt is theirs? Truly it is my fault that has ensnared them.

sentences.zh: 謂九夷其可處，思致免以全生。

translations.literal: I thought the Nine Yi lands could be dwelt in and sought exemption to preserve life.
translations.idiomatic: I thought the barbarian lands of the Nine Yi might shelter us and sought exile to preserve our lives.

sentences.zh: 嗟性命之難遂，乃窘紲於邊亭。

translations.literal: Alas, life and fate were hard to fulfill; then we were bound in fetters at the border post.
translations.idiomatic: Alas, life and fate could not be fulfilled; we were bound in fetters at the border post.

sentences.zh: 亦何忤於天地，備艱危而是丁。

translations.literal: What offense against Heaven and Earth? Yet hardship and peril were what befell us.
translations.idiomatic: What offense had we committed against Heaven and Earth? Yet hardship and peril were what we met.

sentences.zh: 我聞之於昔誥，功彌高而身蹙。

translations.literal: I have heard it in ancient proclamations: the higher the merit, the more constrained the person.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard it said in ancient edicts: the greater the merit, the more perilous one's position.

sentences.zh: 霍芒刺而幸免，卒傾宗而滅族。

translations.literal: Huo Guang had a thorn-like peril yet barely escaped; in the end the clan was toppled and the lineage exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Guang stood amid peril sharp as a thorn yet barely survived; in the end his house was overthrown and his clan exterminated.

sentences.zh: 周歎貴於獄吏，終下蕃而靡鞠。

translations.literal: Zhou Bo lamented at the prison officer's worth and was finally sent down to the borderlands with no further inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Bo was valued only by his jailer in his grief and was finally sent down to the frontier with no further hearing.

sentences.zh: 雖明德之大賢，亦不免於殘戮，懷今憚而忍人，忘向惠而莫復。

translations.literal: Although enlightened and great worthies, they also could not escape mutilation and slaughter; harboring fear of the present and being cruel to others, forgetting past kindness and never returning it.
translations.idiomatic: Even the enlightened and greatest worthies could not escape mutilation and slaughter; fearing the present, they were cruel to others and forgot past kindness, never to return it.

sentences.zh: 績無賞而震主，將何方以自牧。

translations.literal: Merit without reward shakes the lord; by what direction can one govern oneself?
translations.idiomatic: Merit without reward shakes the ruler; by what course can one restrain oneself?

sentences.zh: 非砏石之圜照，孰違禍以取福，著殷鑒於自古，豈獨歎於季叔。

translations.literal: If not for the polished stone's round reflection, who could turn from disaster to seek fortune? The lesson of Yin is established from antiquity—how can one sigh only for Ji Kang?
translations.idiomatic: Had there been no mirror of polished stone, who could turn from disaster to seek fortune? The warning of Yin has stood since antiquity—why sigh only for Ji Kang?

sentences.zh: 能安親而揚名，諒見稱於先哲。

translations.literal: Able to comfort parents and spread one's name—surely praised by sages of old.
translations.idiomatic: To comfort one's parents and win a good name—surely this was praised by the sages of old.

sentences.zh: 保歸全而終孝，傷在余而皆缺。

translations.literal: To preserve return intact and fulfill filial piety to the end—injury rests in me; all is incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: To return home whole and fulfill filial duty to the end—the wound is mine alone, and all is left incomplete.

sentences.zh: 辱歷世之平素，忽盛滿而傾滅。

translations.literal: A disgrace to generations of ordinary living; suddenly full to overflowing, then toppled and extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: A disgrace to generations of plain living—suddenly brimming full, then overturned and extinguished.

sentences.zh: 惟烝嘗與灑掃，痛一朝而永絕。

translations.literal: Only the seasonal sacrifices and sweeping the graves—pained that in one morning they are forever cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Only the seasonal offerings and sweeping the graves remain—and I grieve that in a single morning they are cut off forever.

sentences.zh: 問其誰而為之，實孤人之險戾。

translations.literal: Ask who did this—it was truly the cruel perversity of the lone man.
translations.idiomatic: Ask who brought this about—it was truly the cruel perversity of this solitary wretch.

sentences.zh: 罪有踰於丘山，雖萬死其何雪。

translations.literal: Crimes exceeding hills and mountains—even ten thousand deaths, how could they be wiped clean?
translations.idiomatic: My guilt exceeds hills and mountains—even ten thousand deaths could not wipe it clean.

sentences.zh: 羈角偃兮衡閭，親朋交兮平義。

translations.literal: In youth at the village gate, kin and friends joined in plain righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: In youth we played at the village gate; kin and friends joined us in plain righteousness.

sentences.zh: 雖履尚兮不一，隆分好兮情寄。

translations.literal: Though conduct and esteem differed, we held close affection as if one heart.
translations.idiomatic: Though our paths and stations differed, we held close in affection as though of one heart.

sentences.zh: 俱憚耕兮從祿，睹世道兮艱詖。

translations.literal: All feared farming and followed stipends, seeing the age's way as hard and crooked.
translations.idiomatic: We all shrank from the plow and sought official stipends, seeing the age's way as hard and crooked.

sentences.zh: 規志局兮功名，每謂之兮為易。

translations.literal: Scheming ambitions confined to merit and fame—we always said it would be easy.
translations.idiomatic: Our ambitions were bounded by merit and fame—we always said success would come easily.

sentences.zh: 今定諡兮闔棺，慚明智兮昔議。

translations.literal: Now posthumous title is set and the casket closed—we are ashamed before the wise judgments of old days.
translations.idiomatic: Now my posthumous title is fixed and the coffin closed—I am ashamed before the wise counsel we once gave.

sentences.zh: 雖待盡兮為恥，嗟厚顏兮靡置。

translations.literal: Though waiting for death is shameful, alas, too thick-faced to find a place.
translations.idiomatic: Though awaiting death is shameful, alas, I am too shameless to find any refuge.

sentences.zh: 長揖兮數子，謝爾兮明智。

translations.literal: Long bow to you, several friends—I thank you for your wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: A long bow to you, my friends—I thank you for your wisdom.

sentences.zh: 百齡兮浮促，終焉兮斟克。

translations.literal: A hundred years float and rush; in the end one weighs and fulfills.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred years float past in haste; in the end each must weigh his measure and be content.

sentences.zh: 臥盡兮斧斤，理命兮同得。

translations.literal: Lying down to exhaust the axe and blade, accepting fate equally obtained.
translations.idiomatic: I lie down to meet the axe and blade, accepting allotted fate as all must.

sentences.zh: 世安彼兮非此，豈曉分兮辨惑。

translations.literal: The age rests in that and not this—how can one discern division and resolve confusion?
translations.idiomatic: The world finds peace in that, not in this—how can one discern the boundary and resolve confusion?

sentences.zh: 御莊生之達言，請承風以為則。

translations.literal: Taking up Zhuangzi's penetrating words, I ask to receive the wind as my model.
translations.idiomatic: I take up Zhuangzi's penetrating words and ask to follow the wind as my guide.

sentences.zh: 周超既降，到彥之以參府事，劉粹遣參軍沈敞之告彥之沙橋之敗，事由周超，彥之乃執之。

translations.literal: After Zhou Chao had surrendered, Dao Yanzhi was handling headquarters affairs; Liu Cui sent staff officer Shen Changzhi to tell Yanzhi that the defeat at Shaqiao was Zhou Chao's doing, and Yanzhi then had him seized.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhou Chao had surrendered, Dao Yanzhi was handling headquarters affairs. Liu Cui sent staff officer Shen Changzhi to inform Yanzhi that the defeat at Shaqiao was Zhou Chao's fault, and Yanzhi had him arrested.

sentences.zh: 先繫皭等，猶未即戮，於是與晦、遯、兄子世基、世猷及同黨孔延秀、周超、費愔、竇應期、蔣虔、嚴千斯等並伏誅。

translations.literal: They had first bound Jiao and the others but not immediately executed them; then Hui, Dun, his nephews Shiji and Shiyou, and fellow conspirators Kong Yanxiu, Zhou Chao, Fei Yin, Dou Yingqi, Jiang Qian, Yan Qiansi, and the rest were all put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao and the others had already been bound but not yet executed; then Hui, Dun, his nephews Shiji and Shiyou, and their fellow conspirators Kong Yanxiu, Zhou Chao, Fei Yin, Dou Yingqi, Jiang Qian, Yan Qiansi, and the rest were all executed.

sentences.zh: 世基，絢之子也，有才氣。

translations.literal: Shiji was the son of Xuan; he had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji was Xuan's son and possessed literary talent.

sentences.zh: 臨死為連句詩曰：「偉哉橫海鱗，壯矣垂天翼。

translations.literal: Facing death he composed linked-verse poetry, saying, "How vast the sea-spanning scale! How mighty the wing that hangs the sky!
translations.idiomatic: Facing death he composed linked verse, saying, "How vast the sea-spanning leviathan! How mighty the wing that hangs the sky!

sentences.zh: 一旦失風水，翻為螻蟻食。」

translations.literal: Once wind and water are lost, it turns instead to food for ants."
translations.idiomatic: Once wind and water are lost, it becomes food for ants instead."

sentences.zh: 晦續之曰：「功遂侔昔人，保退無智力。

translations.literal: Hui continued the verse, saying, "Merit achieved, I matched the men of old; keeping to retreat, I lacked wisdom and strength.
translations.idiomatic: Hui continued, "Merit achieved, I matched the men of old; in knowing when to withdraw, I lacked wisdom and strength.

sentences.zh: 既涉太行險，斯路信難陟。」

translations.literal: Having already crossed the peril of the Taihang range, this road is truly hard to climb."
translations.idiomatic: Having already crossed the peril of the Taihang Mountains, this road is truly hard to ascend."

sentences.zh: 晦死時，年三十七。

translations.literal: When Hui died he was thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was thirty-seven when he died.

sentences.zh: 庾登之、殷道鸞、何承天並皆原免。

translations.literal: Yu Dengzhi, Yin Daoluan, and He Chengtian were all pardoned and spared.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Dengzhi, Yin Daoluan, and He Chengtian were all pardoned and spared.

sentences.zh: 初，河東人商玄石為晦參軍，晦為逆，玄石密欲推西人庾田夫及到彥之從弟為主，田夫等不敢許。

translations.literal: Earlier, Shang Xuanshi of Hedong had served as Hui's staff officer; when Hui rebelled, Xuanshi secretly wished to install the westerner Yu Tianfu and Yanzhi's younger cousin as leader, but Tianfu and the others dared not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Shang Xuanshi of Hedong had served on Hui's staff. When Hui rebelled, Xuanshi secretly wished to install the westerner Yu Tianfu and Yanzhi's younger cousin as leader, but Tianfu and the others dared not consent.

sentences.zh: 玄石知獨謀不立，遂為晦領幢。

translations.literal: Xuanshi knew that acting alone the plot could not succeed, so he then served Hui as standard-bearer.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanshi knew his plot alone could not succeed, so he then served Hui as standard-bearer.

sentences.zh: 事既平，恨本心之不遂，投水死。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, resenting that his original intent had not been fulfilled, he drowned himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion was suppressed, resenting that his original intent had not been fulfilled, he drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉之，以其子懷福為衡陽王義季右軍參軍督護。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor praised him and appointed his son Huai Fu as Right Army Staff Officer and Supervisor on the staff of Prince Yiji of Hengyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor praised his loyalty and appointed his son Huai Fu as Right Army Staff Officer and Supervisor on the staff of Prince Yiji of Hengyang.

sentences.zh: 晦走，左右皆棄之，唯有延陵蓋追隨不舍。

translations.literal: When Hui fled, his attendants all abandoned him; only Yanling Gai followed without leaving.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui fled, his attendants all abandoned him; only Yanling Gai followed and would not leave.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉之，後以蓋為長沙王義欣鎮軍功曹督護。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor praised him, and afterward appointed Gai as Supervisor and Merit Officer on the staff of Prince Yixin of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor praised his loyalty and later appointed Gai as Supervisor and Merit Officer on the staff of Prince Yixin of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：謝晦坐璽封違謬，遂免侍中，斯有以見高祖之識治，宰臣之稱職也。

translations.literal: The historian writes: Because Xie Hui was punished for an error in seal and commission, he was removed as gentleman attendant—thus one may see the High Ancestor's discernment in governance and his chief ministers' fulfillment of duty.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Because Xie Hui was punished for an error in seal and commission and removed as gentleman attendant, one may see the High Ancestor's discernment in governance and his chief ministers' fulfillment of duty.

sentences.zh: 夫孥戮所施，事行重釁，左黜或用，義止輕愆。

translations.literal: Family execution is applied when the offense is a serious crime; demotion may be used, but the principle extends only to minor faults.
translations.idiomatic: Family execution is reserved for serious crimes; demotion may be applied, but only for minor faults.

sentences.zh: 輕愆，物之所輕；

translations.literal: Minor faults are what things are lenient toward;
translations.idiomatic: Minor faults are what the law treats lightly;

sentences.zh: 重釁，人之所重。

translations.literal: serious crimes are what people take seriously.
translations.idiomatic: serious crimes are what people take seriously.

sentences.zh: 故斧鉞希行於世，徽簡日用於朝，雖貴臣細故，不以任隆弛法，至乎下肅上尊，用此道也。

translations.literal: Therefore the axe was rarely wielded in the realm and demotion memos were daily in court; even grand ministers' small matters did not relax the law because of high rank—down to the people's reverence and the ruler's dignity, this was the way used.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore capital punishment was rarely seen in the realm and demotion memos circulated daily at court; even a grand minister's minor offense did not relax the law because of high rank—to secure reverence below and dignity above, this was the principle.

sentences.zh: 自太祖臨務，茲典稍違，網以疏行，法為恩息，妨德害美，抑此之由。

translations.literal: From the time the Founding Emperor took power, this standard was gradually violated; the net ran loose and the law paused for mercy—harm to virtue and injury to excellence arose from this.
translations.idiomatic: From the time the Founding Emperor took power, this standard was gradually abandoned; the net was cast loosely and the law yielded to mercy—harm to virtue and injury to excellence arose from this.

sentences.zh: 降及大明，傾詖愈甚，自非訐竊深私，陵犯密諱，則左降之科，不行於權戚。

translations.literal: Down to the Daoming era, bias grew worse still; unless one committed slander, theft, or deep private crimes, or violated secret taboos, the demotion statute was not applied to powerful kin.
translations.idiomatic: By the Daoming era, favoritism had grown worse still; unless one committed slander, theft, or grave private crimes, or violated imperial taboos, the demotion statute was not applied to the powerful and well connected.

sentences.zh: 若有身觸盛旨，釁非國刑，免書裁至，弔客固望其門矣。

translations.literal: If one merely offended imperial intent, with an offense not warranting national punishment, a pardon edict would barely be needed before condolence callers were already at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: If one merely offended imperial displeasure, with a fault falling short of state punishment, a pardon edict would scarcely be needed before sympathizers were already crowding the gate.

sentences.zh: 由是律無恆條，上多弛行，綱維不舉，而網目隨之。

translations.literal: Thus the law had no constant articles, the ruler often enforced laxly, the main rope was not raised, yet the mesh still followed.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the law had no fixed articles, the ruler often enforced it loosely, the governing framework was not upheld, yet petty regulations still proliferated.

sentences.zh: 所以吉人防著在微，慎大由小，蓋為此云。

translations.literal: Therefore the wise guard against prominence at the subtle level and caution in great matters begins with small ones—it is for this that I say so.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the wise guard against prominence at the subtle level and exercise caution in great matters by beginning with small ones—it is for this that I say so.
